definitions.gloss: insects (as a group); the insect class
definitions.explanation: Insects considered collectively as a category of living things. The suffix {類|るい} groups the members into a class, so the word means insects in general rather than one particular bug.

examples.japanese: {昆虫類|こんちゅうるい}を{観察|かんさつ}する。
この{森|もり}には{多|おお}くの{昆虫類|こんちゅうるい}が{生息|せいそく}している。
examples.english: Many kinds of insects live in this forest.

examples.japanese: {昆虫類|こんちゅうるい}は{地球上|ちきゅうじょう}で{最|もっと}も{種類|しゅるい}が{多|おお}い{生|い}き{物|もの}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Insects are said to be the most diverse group of living things on Earth.

notes:
Formed from {昆虫|こんちゅう} (insect) plus the suffix {類|るい} (kind, class), which groups things into a category. Used when speaking of insects collectively, especially in scientific or descriptive contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {昆虫類|こんちゅうるい}を{採集|さいしゅう}する: to collect insects
- {昆虫類|こんちゅうるい}の{生態|せいたい}: the ecology of insects
- {昆虫類|こんちゅうるい}が{生息|せいそく}する: insects inhabit (a place)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {昆虫|こんちゅう}: insect — refers to an individual insect or insects in general
- {虫|むし}: bug, insect — everyday word, broader and less technical than {昆虫|こんちゅう}
